reason: KeepsExisting makes the result r ++ new. NoDuplicateId keeps rows of r out of new, AddsOnlyAbsent and AddsAllAbsent with distinct starter ids make new hold exactly one row for each absent starter entry, and the three enabled laws fix the enabled flag in every case (enable false, locked, enable true and not locked). NewInStarterOrder then fixes the order, and an Entry has no other field, so two passing designs give the same registry.
